cover: Sort every action your AI can take

slides.title: Ask: what if it's wrong and nobody checks?
slides.body: If the answer is "someone rewrites a draft," the cost is small. If it's "a refund goes out," a person sees it first.

slides.title: Alone: reading, searching, drafting
slides.body: These can get less review when the stakes are low. Check what uses that output next.

slides.title: Prepared by AI, approved by a person
slides.body: Customer emails, record updates, price changes, refunds, official filings. A person reads the result and presses the button.

slides.title: Never: outside its permissions
slides.body: Deleting data, moving money above a set limit, changing permissions. The AI can suggest it, and its permissions block the action.

slides.title: Check the review screen
slides.body: Source beside the draft, editing as easy as approving, unusual items that look unusual, routine ones batched.

slides.title: Revisit the line after a few weeks
slides.body: Output people almost never change can move to spot checks. Kinds that still get edited keep their checkpoint.
